full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
conclusion: The vector space V(K)=M⊗_Z K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is either zero or all of V(K), for all the original parameters including λ=0, p=2, and arbitrary fields K of characteristic p.

parameters.type: complex vector space equipped with a complex sl₂-module structure
additive subgroup of V, with its induced integer-module structure

hypotheses.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

definitions.definition: n=λ.toNat+1, where λ.toNat=max(λ,0) viewed as a natural number; when λ≥0 this is λ+1.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(1/(r! in C)) x^r; composition is the endomorphism product, the zeroth power is the identity.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(1/(r! in C)) y^r.

definitions.type: family of vectors in V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural i, e_i=(1/(i! in C)) y^i v.

definitions.type: integer-valued family indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For natural j, c_j is the integer cast of Nat.choose(λ.toNat,j). For λ≥0 this is binom(λ,j).

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural i,j≤λ.toNat
definitions.definition: A_ij=X_(λ.toNat−i) Y_(λ.toNat) X_(λ.toNat) Y_(λ.toNat−j), with the rightmost factor acting first.
D=∏_(t=0)^(λ.toNat) c_t; an empty product is one.
U=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, the balanced tensor product of integer modules. Its K-action is a·(m⊗b)=m⊗(ab).

definitions.type: induced K-linear operator for a specified lattice-preserving complex-linear operator T
definitions.definition: For any complex-linear T:V→V with T(M)⊆M, T^K:U→U denotes the operator m⊗a↦T(m)⊗a, extended by the balanced tensor relations. This notation asserts no preservation of M by an arbitrary T; preservation must be established in the packet. It applies to x,y,h,X_r,Y_r,A_ij only where their preservation has been supplied or proved.

binders.type: complex-linear endomorphism of V satisfying T(M)⊆M

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra generated by the elements X_r and Y_r for all natural r, acting on V by the specified representation.

L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, equipped, whenever the commutator relations and lattice stability in the original assumptions hold, with their induced commutator bracket and action on U. The bracket normalization is [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, including characteristic 2.
